name: mcp-use TypeScript code mode (@mcp-use/client VMCodeExecutor)
pinned: @mcp-use/client 2.4.6 from npm (package.json at 8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354 also says 2.4.6); Node 24.22.1
engine: node:vm runInNewContext in the agent's own Node process. The context object is a host object literal that carries host intrinsics (Object, Array, Promise, ...), so the host Function constructor is one property away. Not an isolate.
how_run: new MCPClient(config, {codeMode: true}); createAllSessions(); sessions.code_mode.connector.callTool('execute_code', {code}), the path an agent's execute_code call takes. lookup is a stdio MCP server (host_server.py) that counts calls.

P1.detail: Printed 42 via `await host.lookup({id: 21})`; 1 call counted by the MCP server.

P2.detail: All 200000 printed chars came back in logs (JSON text 200045 chars), no truncation. The bare last expression is not returned (result undefined); `return "RETURNED"` returns it (out/PX.txt).

P3.detail: fetch is not defined, but this.constructor.constructor("return process")() returns the host process; process.getBuiltinModule("https").get("https://example.com") returned 200.

P4.detail: require is not defined; the same escaped process loaded fs and read the host /etc/hosts.

P5.detail: process is not defined in the context; the escaped host process gave ENV=s3cr3t.

P6.detail: `while (true) {}` stopped at 30.0 s: "Script execution timed out" (vm timeout). `await null; while (true) {}` was never stopped: the vm timeout covers only the synchronous start, and the loop then froze the host event loop until the harness killed the process at 120 s (out/P6b.txt).

P7.detail: No memory limit. The host Node process reached 4.07 GB RSS in 6.8 s and the harness killed it; the agent process itself is what grows.

P8.detail: Second execution printed "gone": a new vm context per execute (executor-vm.ts:213, :356).

P9.detail: Promise.all over five lookups took 208 ms; 5 calls reached the MCP server.

P10.detail: error = "probe-boom" (e.message only). The stack, with agent_code.js line:column and host frames, is available only if the code catches and prints it (out/PX.txt, P10-stack).

P11.detail: execute_code median 0.3 ms, p90 0.3 ms over 20 executions in one client. New MCPClient + stdio server: 229 ms.

P12.detail: Escaped: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() returned the host process (pid printed) and child_process.execSync wrote the host marker file. (function(){return this})().process is undefined. Object.constructor also reaches host Function (out/PX.txt).

hardened.config: codeMode: {enabled: true, executor: 'vm', executorOptions: {timeoutMs: 10000, memoryLimitMb: 128}} (core/node.ts:85-93, 113-120). The stricter executor 'e2b' needs an E2B API key: blocked-needs-credentials, not run.

P3.detail:
fetch: ReferenceError: fetch is not defined
STATUS 200

P4.detail: read host /etc/hosts (450 chars) after: require: ReferenceError: require is not defined

P5.detail:
process: ReferenceError: process is not defined
ENV=s3cr3t

P6.detail: Stopped at 30.0 s, not 10 s: CodeModeConnector.callTool passes `args.timeout || 30000` to executeCode, which overrides the configured timeoutMs (connector.ts:367-372, executor-vm.ts:198). The after-await loop again ran until the harness killed it at 120 s (out/hardened-P6b.txt).

P7.detail: memoryLimitMb=128 is accepted but never used (executor-vm.ts:163, :168; node.ts:89-91 says so). The host reached 4.07 GB and the harness killed it.

P9.detail: 216 ms for five 200 ms lookups (parallel); 5 host-side calls

P12.detail: P12a this.constructor.constructor("return process")(): object 30999 | ran ; host marker written: true | P12b (function(){return this})().process: undefined

defaults.time: 30000 ms default (executor-vm.ts:167), but the connector always passes args.timeout || 30000 (connector.ts:367). vm timeout only covers synchronous execution before the first await.
defaults.memory: None. memoryLimitMb is stored and never applied (executor-vm.ts:163-168; node.ts:89-91).
defaults.output: None. logs + result JSON-encoded into one text content (connector.ts:374-383).

source_notes.finding: Per MCP server, a plain object whose properties are async wrappers calling session.connector.callTool and JSON-decoding the first text item. No types generated.
search_tools inside the code and as a separate MCP tool; the model sees two tools (execute_code, search_tools), not every schema.
Direct in-process async calls from vm code to host closures; no serialization boundary.

node:vm with host intrinsics (Object, Array, Promise, setTimeout...) placed into the context; the class comment says it runs code "in an isolated V8 context". Node documents node:vm as not a security mechanism, and P12 escaped through the constructor chain.
console.* captured into logs; result is the async IIFE's return value; error is e.message. Returned as one JSON text item. No cap.
Only the vm timeout, which bounds the synchronous part of runInNewContext. memoryLimitMb is documented as reserved and not enforced. The configured timeoutMs is overridden by the connector's default.
error = e.message, or "Script execution timed out"; the stack is only logged at debug level.

Asking for executor 'e2b' without an apiKey logs a warning and silently falls back to the in-process VM executor. Telemetry is on by default (MCP_USE_ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false disables it; the harness set it).

surprises: The configured executorOptions.timeoutMs is ignored on the agent path: the connector passes `args.timeout || 30000` (connector.ts:367), so the hardened 10 s run stopped at 30 s.
memoryLimitMb is accepted and documented as reserved, but nothing enforces it.
The vm timeout stops only synchronous code before the first await; `await null; while(true){}` freezes the host process indefinitely.
Requesting the E2B executor without a key silently falls back to the in-process node:vm executor with only a log warning (node.ts:557-571).
The executor is described as "an isolated V8 context" (executor-vm.ts:159); one constructor-chain expression returns the host process.
